_readme: Walks and the read & watch list for didullman.com/recs/bay-area. Routes are drawn as straight dashed lines between stops (connect-the-dots, not turn-by-turn). A stop with a placeId opens that place's card.

walks.title: Bernal Heights loop
walks.summary: Over the hill and back: coffee and pastries on Cortland, hidden stairways, and the best sunset view in the city.

stops.name: Pinhole Coffee
stops.note: Morning coffee on Cortland.

stops.name: Black Jet Baking Co.
stops.note: Grab baked goods for the walk.

stops.name: Bernal Heights summit
stops.note: Up and over the hill. In the evening, bring United Dumplings takeout and watch the sunset.

stops.name: Esmeralda slides
stops.note: Trace Bernal's western edge, find the hidden stairways, and try the slides.

stops.name: Old Devil Moon
stops.note: Post-sundowner: ODM, the Royal Cuckoo or Barebottle. Pick your poison.

walks.title: Valencia to Dolores Park
walks.summary: Down Valencia (the parallel, bougier version of Mission Street) to a seat on the grass, then back through the murals.

stops.name: Dog Eared Books
stops.note: Our favorite bookstore, and good for a designy gift.

stops.name: Craftsman and Wolves
stops.note: Coffee, bread or a sandwich. If you're extra patient, the famous Tartine is a few blocks over.

stops.name: Dolores Park
stops.note: Grab a seat on the grass and soak up the city views. Depending on the day, you'll see the park come alive.

stops.name: Clarion Alley
stops.note: Murals, plus our friend's mural in the graffiti alley off Caledonia Street.

walks.title: Way out west
walks.summary: Coffee, a bookstore, the beach, then museums and gardens on the way back through Golden Gate Park.

stops.name: Trouble Coffee
stops.note: Get here by Uber. There's a great bookstore next door.

stops.name: Outerlands
stops.note: A few doors down, if you want to make a full brunch of it.

stops.name: Ocean Beach
stops.note: Walk the beach, or bike or scooter the Great Highway.

stops.name: Japanese Tea Garden
stops.note: A natural oasis. The botanical garden is right next door.

stops.name: de Young Museum
stops.note: Get your art fix, and go up the tower for a panoramic view of the city.

walks.title: Lands End
walks.summary: Coffee, a rugged coastal hike inside the city, and a great dinner date.

stops.name: Trouble Coffee
stops.note: Start with coffee and toast.

stops.name: Lands End Lookout
stops.note: Up from Ocean Beach, then follow the trail along the rugged northwest coast to Sea Cliff.

stops.name: Lincoln Park Steps
stops.note: Walk down the picturesque steps.

stops.name: Pizzetta 211
stops.note: Our favorite date-night pizza. Superb Taiwanese is two blocks further.

walks.title: Trek to the Golden Gate
walks.summary: Rugged cliffs and a rare view of the bridge, ending with dinner and a drink in the city. Long, but a very different look at a few SF neighborhoods.

stops.name: Lands End Lookout
stops.note: Start here, or start at the bridge and walk west if the sun is setting.

stops.name: Baker Beach
stops.note: Dirt trails along the cliffs, past Baker and Marshall's beaches.

stops.name: Golden Gate Bridge
stops.note: A rare perspective on the bridge.

stops.name: Crissy Field
stops.note: Down to the water and along the Marina.

stops.name: The Interval
stops.note: End with a drink. Peruvian, Japanese curry or German food are all close by in the Marina.

walks.title: Obligatory Embarcadero
walks.summary: Only the coolest parts of the tourist trail. Rent a scooter (live a little!) and do the touristy things, just don't tell us about it.

stops.name: Ferry Building
stops.note: Midnite Bagel if at all possible, or the farmers market. A ferry to Sausalito or Angel Island is a must if you have time.

stops.name: Fisherman's Wharf
stops.note: Which you will (and should) absolutely hate.

stops.name: The Buena Vista
stops.note: You must (MUST!) have an Irish coffee.

stops.name: City Lights
stops.note: Walk south on Columbus. Don't miss it.

stops.name: Coit Tower
stops.note: The view from the top is chef's kiss. Dinner at China Live or Tony's, or go wild in Chinatown.

walks.title: East Bay fun day
walks.summary: Bagels in Temescal, people-watching at Lake Merritt, and the Cheese Board line in North Berkeley.

stops.name: Beauty's Bagel Shop
stops.note: MacArthur BART. A heavy brunch: add butter-braised greens and/or a sausage patty.

stops.name: Temescal Alley
stops.note: Cute shops in former horse stalls.

stops.name: Lake Merritt
stops.note: Walk north along the lake and people-watch. Saturday farmers market at Grand Lake. Culture nerds: Oakland Museum. Nature lovers: the Rose Garden.

stops.name: Cheese Board Pizza
stops.note: Stand in line for the famous veggie pizza.

stops.name: Comal
stops.note: End on the back patio with a cocktail, or get mochi donuts at Third Culture.

walks.title: Crosstown Trail
walks.summary: Only for the truly walking-obsessed: the trail across the whole city, from Candlestick to Lands End.

readWatch.title: Season of the Witch
readWatch.note: A sprawling, entertaining journey through SF in the turbulent 60s and 70s. An alternative take on the good ol' days, and the roots of today's issues.

readWatch.title: The Last Black Man in San Francisco
SF Chronicle: the homelessness special report
readWatch.note: Context on the city's biggest debate.

readWatch.title: Devs
readWatch.note: Beautifully shot in SF and at UC Santa Cruz, 90 minutes south.

readWatch.title: Vertigo · Dirty Harry · The Birds · The Rock
readWatch.note: The Birds is Bodega Bay, but it counts. And The Rock is somehow vintage now.
